blurb: The smallest sighthound, a slender Italian hare hunter long kept by royalty
description: The Italian Greyhound is a small, slender sighthound from Italy, under 5 kg, with a fine short coat, a high-stepping gait and a long history as a companion.
answer: The Italian Greyhound, or Piccolo Levriero Italiano, is the smallest of the sighthounds and comes from Italy. It stands 32 to 38 cm at the withers and weighs no more than about 5 kg. Bred to hunt hare and rabbit, it is now kept mostly as a companion dog.

body: Small sighthounds have long been popular with European nobility and royalty, from the Medici family to Catherine the Great and Queen Victoria, and they appear in Roman sculpture and in paintings by Giotto and Tiepolo. Dogs of this type reached Britain in the early 19th century, and the AKC began registering them in 1886. The breed came close to extinction during the Second World War and recovered from the 1950s. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1956 under the English name Italian Sighthound.

The Italian Greyhound is deep in the chest, with a tucked-up abdomen, long slender legs, a long neck and a small, narrow head. Its gait is high-stepping with a fast gallop. The coat may be solid black, grey or isabelline in any shade, with white markings accepted only on the chest and feet.

Sources give little detail on the breed's temperament beyond its long role as a companion dog. The American Kennel Club and the UK Kennel Club classify it as a toy breed, while the FCI places it with the sighthounds.

Although small, the breed was developed to hunt and is capable of bursts of speed up to 60 km/h. Sources say little about care routines; owners are generally advised to provide safe, enclosed space where a sighthound can run.

Conditions reported in the breed include congenital deafness and cervical intervertebral disc disease. The Orthopedic Foundation for Animals found it the least affected of 157 breeds by hip dysplasia. Median longevity is reported at about 14 years.

faq.q: How big does an Italian Greyhound get?
faq.a: It stands 32 to 38 cm at the withers and weighs no more than about 5 kg, making it the smallest sighthound.

faq.q: How long do Italian Greyhounds live?
faq.a: Median longevity is reported at about 14 years, compared with about 12.5 years for dogs overall.

faq.q: How fast is an Italian Greyhound?
faq.a: It is capable of bursts of speed up to about 60 km/h (35 mph).

faq.q: Is the Italian Greyhound recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it in 1956 and lists it as the Italian Sighthound, number 200 in Group 10.
